chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them both) were commanded to build the House and its building was completed, Ibrahim sat upon a corner, then called out: 'Come for the Hajj! Come for the Hajj!' Had he called out 'Come all of you to the Hajj!', none would have performed Hajj except those who were in those days human beings in physical form. But he called out: 'Come for the Hajj!' Thus the people responded from within the backs of men: 'Here I am, O Inviter to God! Here I am, O Inviter to God, Mighty and Majestic!'

So whoever responded ten times will perform Hajj ten times, and whoever responded five times will perform Hajj five times, and whoever responded more than that will perform Hajj by that count, and whoever responded once will perform Hajj once, and whoever did not respond will not perform Hajj.

key_terms.أَصْلَابِ الرِّجَالِ: The backs/loins of men — referring to the pre-existent realm where souls await physical creation
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: Labbayk — the talbiyah response meaning 'Here I am in answer to your call', echoed in Hajj rituals to this day
key_terms.هَلُمَّ الْحَجَّ: Come for the Hajj — the singular imperative form used by Ibrahim, enabling souls in the spiritual realm to respond

ai.seo_question: Why did Ibrahim call 'Come for the Hajj' rather than 'Come all of you to the Hajj'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates the cosmological origins of the Hajj pilgrimage, teaching that when Prophet Ibrahim (AS) completed the Kaaba and called humanity to Hajj, souls still in the loins of their ancestors heard and responded. The phrasing of Ibrahim's call ('Come for the Hajj!' rather than a second-person plural) was divinely ordered so that pre-existent souls across all of time could respond. This hadith grounds the Hajj obligation in a primordial covenant: the number of times a person performs Hajj in their lifetime corresponds to the number of times their soul responded to Ibrahim's call in the pre-creational realm.
